title: fix(cl): the opening rapid starts over its entry point; the clearance plane must clear the stock and the fixtures
body:
## What changed

1. **Seat (from the held commit `edd41f0f5`).** The opening rapid of a clearance-seeded milling path starts over its own entry X/Y on the clearance plane (`cl::Toolpath::seat_approach(seed)`). It does not start at the WCS origin (#2382's seat, reversed) or at the frame zero. The end of the rapid does not change, so no posted block changes.
2. **First-traverse law (new).** After a tool change the machine does not know its X/Y. The post sends Z to the clearance plane and then X/Y at that plane, so that traverse can cross any point of the setup. The new law `sim::verify::first_traverse_low` gives the blocking verdict `Warning::FirstTraverseLow { at, height_mm, top_mm, fixture }`. The start height of the path must be at or above the top of the start stock and the top of each fixture, in the frame of the operation.
   - The stock top is the full start stock, not the in-process stock.
   - A 3+2 plane reads the eight corners of each box along its tool axis. It does not read the machine table slab (`MAX_FIXTURE_DIM` wide): along a tilted axis that slab gives a "top" of about 1e6 mm. Upright frames read the table. The first traverse of a 3+2 operation against the machine table is thus not judged: #2987 (P1) owns that gap.
   - Scope: 2D milling, 3D milling and vertical hole kinds on a mill without a rotary axis, upright or 3+2. The rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds have no such law yet: #2965 (P1).
   - The rule is in `camcraft-sim` (it owns `Warning` and `FixtureBox`). `app` passes the extents in `operation/first_traverse.rs`. `generate.rs` gets two calls. MCP names the verdict `first_traverse_low`. No new crate dependency.
   - Reuse check: no existing law blocks this case on every path. `RapidInStock` needs a known line. The "Clearance in stock:" note does not block. The `grblhal` and `tinyg` posts refuse only for the stock, and only in those two posts.
3. **Words.** The door word at creation and the "Clearance in stock:" note no longer offer "face the stock first" as the fix (a face does not lift the first traverse over the start stock).
4. **Cache.** The op stamp salt changes from `v3` to `v4`. Old caches read Stale once.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/2901-first-traverse-law.md`.

## Site and guide (review round 1)

- `site/tests/test_guide_images.py` pins the regenerated counts: `Indexed Face1` `{gouge: 30, first_traverse_low: 1}`, `Swarf1` `shank_hit: 884` (was 897).
- `site/content/guide/multi-axis/indexed.md` names the first-traverse-low warning and says what it means and how to fix it. `site/content/guide/multi-axis/operations-multiaxis.md` states 884 shank hits.
- `site/content/guide/reference/troubleshooting.md` no longer tells the user to face the stock first for a clearance plane inside the stock. It has a new entry for the first-traverse message: its text, its meaning and its fix.

## Readings

- WCS at the stock corner and at the stock centre (`wcs_start`): Face1, Finish1 and Drill1 give the same moves for the two WCS positions. The opening rapid has no X/Y travel and starts on the clearance plane over the entry. No move reaches the world origin. The first posted X/Y block is the entry less G54.
- Before: the opening rapid of Face1 started at the G54 corner (40, 20) at Z 30 and travelled to the entry. After: it starts and ends over the entry.

## Refusal texts

- Stock: `Op1Contour: the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown X/Y at the clearance height Z8.000, under the stock top at Z10.000 - raise the clearance height above Z10.000`
- Fixture: `Face1: the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown X/Y at the clearance height Z30.000, under the fixture top at Z40.000 - raise the clearance height above Z40.000`

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/first_traverse.rs` (new):
  - `a_far_clamp_over_the_clearance_plane_holds_the_post_by_name`
  - `the_same_clamp_under_the_clearance_plane_posts` (the control: the program is byte-identical to the program with no clamp)
  - `a_3_2_plane_reads_the_stock_top_along_its_tool_axis` (B 10 deg: refused at Z 25, posts at Z 30)
  - `the_simulation_opens_over_the_entry_on_the_clearance_plane`
- The stock case (Z 8 under Z 10): `stale_rapid_law::regenerating_the_old_cache_judges_it_under_the_new_law`.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/first_traverse.rs`: 4 unit tests (stock, far fixture, at-or-above passes, tilted corners).
- The pins of `edd41f0f5` stay green: `wcs_start` (6), `origin_approach` (8).

## Changed test expectations and goldens

No expectation is weaker. Details are in the decision file.

- `stale_rapid_law`: `RapidInStock { at: 0 }` -> `FirstTraverseLow { at: 0, height_mm: 8.0, top_mm: 10.0, fixture: false }`, and the refusal must name the op and both heights. The same program is refused at the same move for the same cause.
- `clearance_in_stock`: 4 cases name the new verdict in place of `RapidInStock { at: 0 }`. One case reverses (the known cost): `the_same_plane_over_stock_an_earlier_face_cut_down_is_air_and_posts` -> `..._holds_only_for_the_first_traverse`. The traverses inside the path are still acquitted by the face ahead, but the first traverse holds the post. The door word now says "raise Clearance to the stock top or above".
- `wcs_start` clamp test (held work): the 40 mm clamp on the old origin-to-entry line gets no struck-move verdict and no routed link. Only the first-traverse verdict holds the post.
- `operations` (slot helper): the Z 5 plane in a 20 mm block is now the first-traverse verdict, not the "Clearance in stock" note.
- `stock_source_holes` framed B 10 deg chamfer: the clearance changes from 25 to 30. The tilted block's corner is at 25.77 along the tool axis.
- `center_cut_owed`: the expected facer path gets the same seat.
- `stock_play`, UI `sim_readout_names_the_op_and_the_verb`: the zero-length opening segment takes no time.
- `regression_models` minutes: `0.35983333 -> 0.35933333` and `1.47475343 -> 1.46766667` (no opening travel from the frame zero).
- `deburr_cache_stamp`, `wire_stamp`: stamp pins recaptured under salt v4.
- CL goldens, only the `START` line changes. Each new value is the end of the opening rapid:
  - `circular_ramp_stay_down`
  - `contour_start_point`
  - `pocket_waterline_square_dogbone`
  - `pocket3d_trochoidal_pocket`
  - `pocket_rest_corners`
  - `pocket_adaptive_v63` (read with `include_str!`; I edited this one line by hand)
  - `thread_mill_external_m10_single_form`
  - `thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form`
- **No NC golden changes.**

## Example projects (regenerated, `.nc` byte-identical)

These projects were loaded, then each operation was regenerated with `GenerateOperation` and the project was saved with `project::save`:
- `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj`
- `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj`
- `examples/first-router-part.camproj`
- `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj` (by the maintainer's answer)

The diff is the stamps, the start of the opening rapid, the file version and the tool `number` fields. In `guide-multiaxis`, the Swarf1 cache also moves by one rounding step in 402 coordinates, and its shank-hit list follows the current law (897 -> 884; the changed moves are 639-1010, inside the path).

The committed `.nc` files do not change (`git diff` shows no `.nc` file). The continuous test's `WRITE_GOLDEN` path would rewrite 7 A-words by one last digit, so I did not use it.

The two operations of `guide-multiaxis` were blocked before (gouges, shank hits) and stay blocked. Indexed Face1 also gets the first-traverse verdict.

## Known cost

An operation whose clearance plane is under the stock top or a fixture top on purpose is refused, for example a contour after a face took the whole top down. The message says to raise the clearance height.

In the tests this law changed 9 tests in 5 files, all fixtures inside `crates/*/tests`. Only one of them went from "posts" to "refused". No catalog case and no shipped `.nc` stopped posting.

## Gate

- The quick gate falls back to batch (`crates/cl` changed).
- One full pass on `6ae9b6a77`: debug builds plus the cl, motion, sim, post, app and ui suites, 929 steps, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=18`. 926 steps passed. The 3 red steps (4 failing tests) are fixed in `806aa0cf9`.
- On `806aa0cf9`, after `git merge origin/main`, these passed:
  - `catalog_groove_part_off`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_edge_work`
  - `first_traverse`, `stale_rapid_law`, `wcs_start`, `stock_play`, `wire_stamp`
  - `first_4axis_part`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `first_router_part`
  - `golden_cl`, `fixture_route`, `tilt_basis_compat`, `clearance_in_stock`, `operations`, `center_cut_owed`, `regression_models`, `stock_source_holes`, `thread_boss`, `solid_law_goldens`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `index_swing`, `deburr_cache_stamp`, `pocket_no_adaptive`, `rest_pocket`, `pocket3d_trochoid`, `circular_stay_down`, `contour_start_point`, `corner_relief`
  - `camcraft-cl` `origin_approach`, the `camcraft-sim` lib tests, and the `camcraft-ui` lib tests (1290 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The site tests ran with Python only (`python -m unittest discover -s site/tests`). The Zola build tests need `zola` on `PATH` and did not run. The other red site tests (`test_guide_icons` act-report icon, `test_first_4axis_part` and `test_first_continuous_4axis_part` bold-label checks, and the Zola errors) are red on `origin/main` too.
- Known: `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs` is 471 lines (it was 460, already over 400).
- Known: `stock_play::the_transport_maps_onto_the_plan_by_name` accepts either opening outcome. A stricter pin needs a build; the coordinator schedules it.

- The release heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run.
- The full batch did not run on the final head after the second merge of main. The coordinator runs it.
- No machine run.

Changelog: The opening rapid of a milling operation now starts over its own entry point instead of the WCS origin. The program is refused by name when the clearance plane is not above the stock top and every fixture top, because the first rapid after a tool change comes from an unknown X/Y. Saved toolpaths regenerate once.

Effort: max (escalated from high)

Refs #2902

Refs #2987
